subject: Staged traffic scenarios for Demo Day — quota ask & fallback plan
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aurora Health Technical Ops <ops@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Demo Day traffic heads-up + request for temporary uplift

Hi Marcus / team,

Quick note — our marketing team just confirmed a scheduled Demo Day for Dec 7 where we'll stream a live product demo to ~120k registered attendees (expectation: ~4k concurrent calls to your inference endpoints during peak demo segments). This is a one-hour event with two major demo moments at 10:15 and 10:45 PT.

Request: can Redwood provide a temporary quota uplift or a short-term burst policy for the Dec 7 demo window (09:45–11:15 PT)? We need a plan that avoids token throttling for the demo and a fallback if we hit limits. We have limited time to test, so leaning on Redwood's recommended staging approach.

I've attached our preliminary traffic scenarios (simple numbers) and ops contacts. Please loop in whatever infra/product folks are needed.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Partnerships, Aurora Health
attach: aurora_demo_traffic_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo Day traffic heads-up + request for temporary uplift

Kimberly / Neha / Aditya — forwarding Aurora's ask (see attached). Short timeline: Dec 7, two spikes in a ~1.5h window. Elaine's expecting ~4k concurrent inference requests at peak.

Can we:
- Confirm if a short-term quota uplift is feasible under Dedicated/Hosted for this account (and any guardrails).
- Propose a staged throttling/canary plan we can run on Dec 6 (smoke + scaled test) to validate fallbacks.
- Identify any product asks (e.g., temporary cache warm-up, prefix caching enablement, or token caps) we should document for Aurora.

I'll coordinate with Aurora on times for a quick run on Dec 6. Need a recommendation + estimated lead time by EOD Mon (Nov 30).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo Day traffic heads-up + request for temporary uplift

Thanks Marcus — quick framing from CS: Aurora is a strategic mid-market account (on Hosted with usage commitment). We should prioritize reliability for this event; downside is high if demo hits throttling.

Product asks / immediate asks for infra:
- A temporary 3x concurrent request uplift for the 09:45–11:15 PT window on Dec 7 (with immediate rollback at 11:30).
- Enable prefix/KV cache for the two demo prompts (they'll send identical example prompts during the demo).
- If uplift isn't possible at that scale on Hosted, propose a short Dedicated burst for the 2h window and confirm support coverage.

Please see attached scenario sheet from Aurora (they already included two traffic curves). I'll be the point for scheduling the Dec 6 smoke test.

attach: capacity_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo Day traffic heads-up + request for temporary uplift

Folks — technical summary and constraints: we can support a temporary uplift but need to define the mechanism and rollback. Options:

1) Hosted temporary cap bump — quickest operational path if Aurora's account tier allows manual uplift. Ops will provision a rate window and an automated rollback. Expected lead time: ~24–36 hours to schedule and validate. Risk: broader capacity contention during other customer peaks.

2) Short Dedicated burst (recommended for guaranteed headroom) — spin up a small dedicated GPU pool for a 2.5h window. Lead time: ~48–72 hours; involves commit/approval for burst cost. Pros: deterministic latency and no cross-tenant impact.

Tech asks for Aurora (action items we should confirm with them):
- Exact token-per-request distribution (avg tokens/inference + expected response lengths).
- Confirm the two canonical prompts to enable prefix/KV caching; we need them by Dec 4 to pre-warm caches.
- Run a staged smoke test on Dec 6: step 1 (100 reqs/s for 5 min), step 2 (500 reqs/s for 10 min), step 3 (target concurrency window for 15 min). We'll need an ops contact and a call to monitor metrics.

If Aurora can't provide token distribution, we should build conservative headroom assumptions: assume 200 tokens avg/request. For 4k concurrent requests that becomes ~800k tokens/minute at peak — significant but feasible with a Dedicated burst.

I'll draft the burst runbook and the exact rollback playbook. Marcus / Kimberly — can you confirm budgetary approval for a short Dedicated burst or whether they want to try Hosted uplift first?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Infrastructure Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo Day traffic heads-up + request for temporary uplift

All — consolidated plan and next steps:

1) Immediate (by EOD Dec 1): Marcus to confirm Aurora preference (Hosted uplift vs Dedicated burst) and budget sign-off.
2) By Dec 4: Aurora to provide canonical prompts + token-per-request estimate.
3) Dec 6 (10:00–12:00 PT): Staged smoke test (Aditya to run test runbook, Kimberly to coordinate Aurora ops).
4) Dec 7 (09:00 PT prep; 09:45–11:15 active window): Implement chosen uplift, monitoring runbook active, CS on standby.

Attachments: I've uploaded a shared runbook (link below) and endorsed Aditya's conservative token assumption for planning until Aurora provides exact numbers.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-demo/aurora-demo-day

If everyone is aligned I'll send a short note to Aurora with the recommended approach and draft runbook.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
